Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1226 PM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE NORTHEAST...NORTHWEST NEBRASKA INTO SOUTH-CENTRAL SOUTH
DAKOTA...NORTHWEST OKLAHOMA INTO SOUTHWEST MISSOURI...

...SUMMARY...
A few strong storms may occur over small parts of the Great Plains,
and over the Northeast on Thursday with locally strong wind gusts.
Isolated hail may occur with the Northern Plains/Ozarks activity.

...Northwest Oklahoma into southwest Missouri...
A stalled surface boundary is expected to be draped across southern
Kansas into central Missouri. The Missouri portion of the boundary
will likely be reinforced by early day convection/cloud cover.
Strong heating south of the boundary will allow for locally enhanced
surface convergence. Storm development is possible along the
boundary, though it remains uncertain where this development is most
probable. The presence of the broad trough to the north will support
sufficient shear that storms would be at least marginally organized.
Damaging wind gusts will likely be the main threat with this
activity with marginal hail possible where buoyancy will be locally
greater in Missouri.

...Northeast...
Areas of modest to strong heating of a very moist (70+ F dewpoints)
airmass will support 1500-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE by mid-afternoon.
Deep-layer shear will not be overly strong, but enhanced mid-level
winds associated with the Great Lakes trough will promote marginally
organized clusters/linear segments. Isolated wind damage will be
possible with this activity.

...Nebraska/South Dakota...
A secondary cold front will develop within the northern Plains.
Moisture return ahead of the boundary will bring upper 50s to low
60s F dewpoint northward. Mid-level heights are forecast to rise
slightly during the period. Given effective shear of around 40 kt
across the boundary, an isolated supercell or two will be possible
where surface heating can remove MLCIN. Severe winds and marginally
severe hail would be the expected hazards. The Marginal risk remains
where confidence in storm development is highest, though a storm or
two could develop farther northeast. Confidence remains too low for
an expansion of probabilities.

..Wendt.. 08/05/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0234 PM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PARTS OF THE
UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...

...SUMMARY...
A few strong storms may occur over parts of the Upper Mississippi
Valley region on Friday. Locally strong/damaging wind gusts appear
most likely.

...Upper Mississippi Valley...
An intensifying mid-level jet is expected to move into the northern
Plains/Upper Midwest during the afternoon. Convergence along a cold
front should increase within Minnesota/western Wisconsin/Iowa. With
around 40 kt of effective shear, supercell structures are possible
at least initially. With time, convergence along the front may
promote more linear storm modes with one or more organizing
clusters/line segments. The zone of greater buoyancy will not extend
much to the east into Wisconsin. There will be a reservoir of strong
instability in parts of Iowa, however. A small MCS could organize
and move southward into this airmass. Wind damaging will be the
primary hazard, though large hail could occur with initial
supercells.

...Upper Ohio Valley into Mid-Atlantic...
Upper 60s to potentially mid 70s F dewpoints are forecast to remain
across these regions into Friday. Stronger surface heating and
temperatures at or above 90 F in some locations will support
1500-2500 J/kg MLCAPE. Deep-layer shear across the
Mid-Atlantic/Northeast is expected to be a bit weaker than on
Thursday. Scattered thunderstorms are probable by the afternoon.
Generally weak winds throughout the troposphere suggest locally
pulse severe storms. Lack of greater organization precludes a risk
area at this time.

Stronger mid-level flow is forecast across the Upper Ohio Valley in
association with the Great Lakes trough and possibly an MCV moving
eastward. Models differ on the timing/strength of pertinent surface
features during the afternoon. A zone of greater storm organization
could develop from eastern Indiana into parts of central southern
Ohio and northern Kentucky. Uncertainty remains too high for
probabilities.

..Wendt.. 08/05/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0400 AM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 081200Z - 131200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Saturday/D4...
Southwest midlevel winds of only 25 kt will exist across the
Northeast, while low-level moisture remains in place supporting up
to 2000 J/kg MUCAPE with poor lapse rates aloft. This will support
daytime thunderstorms over a large area from the Appalachians into
the Northeast, and a few severe gusts cannot be ruled out.
Otherwise, normal gusty outflow winds are to be expected.

To the west, an area of stronger instability is forecast across the
Mid MO Valley, where northwesterly midlevel winds of 35 kt will
exist along the southern periphery of a trough sweeping across the
Upper Great Lakes. Evening/overnight storms may occur across parts
of eastern NE, IA, and MO, and instability may be large enough to
warrant at least low severe probabilities as the event nears in
time.

...Sunday/D5...
Drying will occur aloft over parts of the Northeast as a wave moves
into Quebec, but substantial low-level moisture will still support
scattered thunderstorms ahead of a cold front across the Mid
Atlantic. Shear will again be weak, but perhaps enough mean wind
speeds will exist for storms to be mobile/produce areas of strong
gusts.

To the west, low-level moisture is forecast to shift a bit farther
north into the Dakotas, and this will occur beneath stronger
northwest flow aloft. This area bears watching in later outlooks, as
wind profiles may somewhat favor supercells. Predictability is
currently low.

...Mon/D6 to Wed/D8...
While predictability decreases further during this time frame,
moderate west to northwest flow aloft will remain from the upper MS
Valley across the Great Lakes, which will spread into the Northeast
D7/D8. If a wave does amplify within this flow regime, a corridor of
damaging winds could develop given upper 60s to low 70s F dewpoints
along/south of the mean frontal zone (roughly IA to NY/PA by end of
the period). Model variation is currently too great to depict an
precise corridor.

..Jewell.. 08/05/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0744 PM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 060100Z - 061200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE CENTRAL PLAINS...OZARKS...MID MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...SOUTHERN HIGH
PLAINS AND SOUTHERN ARIZONA....

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts and hail will be possible this
evening in parts of the central Plains, Ozarks, mid Mississippi
Valley, southern High Plains and southern Arizona.

...Central Plains/Ozarks/Mid Mississippi Valley...
The latest water vapor imagery shows a broad area of cyclonic flow
over the north-central U.S., with an embedded shortwave trough in
the mid Mississippi Valley. At the surface, an ill-defined front is
located from far southern Kansas northeastward into Missouri and
Illinois. Scattered thunderstorms are ongoing on the cool side of
the boundary in northern Missouri. Along and to the south of the
front, surface dewpoints are in the 70s F, and the RAP has MLCAPE in
the 1500 to 2500 J/kg range. In addition, the WSR-88D VWP at St.
Louis has 0-6 km shear around 30 knots, and veering winds with
height in the lowest 1 Km above ground level. This environment will
be sufficient for isolated severe wind gusts and hail this evening.
However, forecast soundings have poor lapse rates which will keep
any severe threat localized.

...Southern High Plains...
Mid-level flow is west-northwesterly over much of the High Plains
this evening. A small pocket of moderate instability is analyzed by
the RAP over southeastern Colorado. Thunderstorms are ongoing to the
south of the instability max over northeastern New Mexico. These
storms will move east-southeastward into the northwestern Texas
Panhandle and western Oklahoma Panhandle this evening. MLCAPE around
1000 J/kg with 0-6 km shear in the 30 to 40 knot range, along with
steep low to mid-level lapse rates could be enough for isolated
severe gusts and hail.

...Southern Arizona...
The latest RAP analysis shows moderate instability over most of
southern Arizona, where MLCAPE is estimated in the 1000 to 2000 J/kg
range. Thunderstorms are developing in the higher terrain of eastern
Arizona, and these storms will move west-southwestward across
southern Arizona this evening. RAP forecast sounding at Tuscon early
this evening have 0-3 km lapse rates in the 8 to 8.5 C/km range,
along with surface temperature-dewpoint spreads exceeding 30 degrees
F. This will contribute to a potential for isolated severe gusts in
southern Arizona over the next few hours...see MCD 1838.

..Broyles.. 08/06/2026
